generators.name: Analog
generators.description: Analog is a meta-framework for Angular, built on Vite and Nitro, that prerenders file-based routes to static HTML.
generators.notes: firstRelease from npm @analogjs/platform creation (2022-11-17). Markdown rendering is the official @analogjs/content package (marked). Built with static prerender of every post route and no SSR server.

generators.name: Astro
generators.description: Astro is a web framework that renders component-based pages to static HTML at build time.
generators.notes: GitHub's license API returns NOASSERTION; MIT verified from the LICENSE file, packages/astro/package.json and the npm registry. firstRelease from npm astro creation (2021-03-13); the oldest GitHub release is 2021-08-05. MDX is the official @astrojs/mdx integration; this setup uses Markdown only.

generators.name: Cecil
generators.description: Cecil is a PHP static site generator that turns Markdown content and Twig templates into a static website.
generators.notes: Installed from Packagist as cecil/cecil.

generators.name: Cobalt
generators.description: Cobalt is a static site generator written in Rust that renders Markdown with Liquid templates.
generators.notes: Posts are generated without front matter (Cobalt rejects the canonical keys); date and title come from the file name. firstRelease from the first cobalt-bin crate on crates.io (0.2.0, 2016-06-25).

generators.name: DocFX
generators.description: DocFX is a .NET static site generator for documentation that builds Markdown conceptual pages and API reference through Mustache templates.
generators.notes: Benchmarked with a minimal custom template (single conceptual page template, no navbar, TOC, search or affix) instead of the default template. DocFX cannot list pages from a page, so build_command first runs mkindex.sh, which writes index.md from the posts' front matter (part of the timed build).

generators.name: Docusaurus
generators.description: Docusaurus is a React-based static site generator from Meta for documentation sites and blogs, with MDX support.
generators.notes: Version 3.10.2. Blog-only setup: docs plugin off, blog at /posts with a bare Layout override (no navbar/footer), prev/next overridden to null, tags cleared via processBlogPosts (no tag pages), built-in list page emptied, and a small local plugin feeding the index page.

generators.name: dumi
generators.description: dumi is a React-based static site generator for component libraries and documentation, built on Umi, that turns Markdown into static HTML pages.
generators.notes: firstRelease from npm dumi creation (2019-12-27). This setup pins dumi 2.4.50 and overrides the default theme layout (.dumi/theme/layouts/DocLayout) with a bare one: no navbar, sidebar, TOC, search or footer; it renders only the post, and the index page lists all posts.

generators.name: Eleventy
generators.description: Eleventy is a simpler static site generator that transforms a directory of templates into HTML.
generators.notes: The upstream repository was renamed from 11ty/eleventy to 11ty/buildawesome (the project is now branded Build Awesome (Eleventy)); the npm package is still @11ty/eleventy. GitHub's homepage field is https://build.awesome.me/; the Eleventy docs site 11ty.dev, also listed in the package.json homepage, is used here. firstRelease from the oldest GitHub release (v0.2.2, 2018-01-09) and npm 0.2.0 (2018-01-09). Nunjucks is used here; Eleventy also supports other template languages.

generators.name: Gatsby
generators.description: Gatsby is a React-based framework that builds static sites from data sources through a GraphQL data layer.
generators.notes: Markdown is handled by the official gatsby-transformer-remark plugin (used here); MDX by gatsby-plugin-mdx.

generators.name: Hakyll
generators.description: Hakyll is a static site generator library written in Haskell; a site is a compiled Haskell program that renders Markdown through Pandoc and templates.
generators.notes: Pandoc is linked into the site binary, so Markdown needs no external helper.

generators.name: Hexo
generators.description: Hexo is a Node.js static blog framework that renders Markdown posts with themeable templates.
generators.notes: firstRelease from npm hexo creation (2012-10-07); the oldest GitHub release is 1.0.0 (2013-07-04). Markdown via hexo-renderer-marked and EJS via hexo-renderer-ejs, both first-party plugins.

generators.name: Hugo
generators.description: Hugo is a static site generator written in Go that renders Markdown content through Go templates.
generators.notes: contentFormats lists formats Hugo renders without external helpers; AsciiDoc, Pandoc and reStructuredText need external executables.

generators.name: Ink
generators.description: Ink is a static blog generator written in Go that renders Markdown posts with YAML front matter through Go templates.
generators.runtime: Go binary (built from the pinned upstream commit)

benchmark.buildCommand: sh -c 'mkdir -p source/post && awk -f convert.awk content/post/*.md && ink build'

generators.notes: Ink publishes no versions: its only release is the rolling nightly tag, so the image builds upstream commit f9aeb2b (2026-06-08) and the version is recorded as nightly-f9aeb2b. The license is CC BY-NC 4.0 per the README (no LICENSE file; GitHub reports none). firstRelease is the repository creation year (2015). The build command converts the generated posts for Ink (drops the leading front matter fence, rewrites the date) in one awk pass before ink build.

generators.name: Jekyll
generators.description: Jekyll is a blog-aware Ruby static site generator that renders Markdown with Liquid templates.
generators.notes: firstRelease from the oldest git tag v0.1.3 (2008-12-07).

generators.name: Jigsaw
generators.description: Jigsaw is a PHP static site generator by Tighten that builds sites with Laravel's Blade templates and Markdown.
generators.notes: Installed from Packagist as tightenco/jigsaw.

generators.name: Lektor
generators.description: Lektor is a Python static content management system that builds sites from per-page contents.lr files, data models and Jinja2 templates.

benchmark.buildCommand:
bash -c 'rm -rf content/posts/*/; set -- posts/*.md; [ -e "$1" ] || exit 1; d=("${@##*/}"); d=("${d[@]%.md}"); d=("${d[@]/#/content/posts/}"); mkdir "${d[@]}"; for f; do n=${f##*/}; n=${n%.md}; IFS= read -r -d "" body < "$f"; printf "_model: post
---
title: %s
---
body:

%s
" "$n" "$body" > content/posts/$n/contents.lr; done; lektor build -O _site --buildstate-path .lektor-cache'

generators.notes: Lektor reads one contents.lr per page, so the timed build_command first converts each generated posts/<name>.md into content/posts/<name>/contents.lr with bash builtins only (one mkdir, one read and one printf per post, no per-post forks). Minimal custom models and templates; build state is written to .lektor-cache.

generators.name: Lume
generators.description: Lume is a static site generator for Deno that builds sites from Markdown and a choice of template engines.
generators.notes: Runs on Deno, not Node.js. Lume is imported from CDN URL https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lumeland/lume@3.3.2/ (pinned in src/deno.json, lockfile src/deno.lock); all remote and npm modules are cached into DENO_DIR at image build, so the timed `deno task build` (run with --cached-only --frozen) is offline. Post URLs keep the date prefix of the file name (/posts/YYYY-MM-DD-N/). Vento is Lume's default template engine.

generators.name: Marmite
generators.description: Marmite is a Rust command-line static site generator for blogs that turns a folder of Markdown files into a site with Tera templates.
generators.runtime: Rust binary (x86_64 release tarball; built from source on arm64)
generators.notes: Benchmarked with minimal templates (base, content, list, group) and search, JSON feeds, sitemap, urls.json, Markdown sources, table of contents, related posts and next/previous links disabled. Marmite still writes tag, author, archive, stream and series pages, RSS feeds and its stock static files; none can be turned off by configuration. firstRelease from the first GitHub release (0.1.4, 2024-10-20).

generators.name: mdBook
generators.description: mdBook is a Rust command-line tool that builds online books from Markdown files listed in a SUMMARY.md, with Handlebars templates.

benchmark.buildCommand:
sh -c 'for f in src/posts/*.md; do [ -e "$f" ] || continue; b=${f##*/}; b=${b%.md}; printf "%s
" "- [$b](posts/$b.md)"; done > src/.list && { printf "# Summary

[Index](README.md)

"; cat src/.list; } > src/SUMMARY.md && { printf "# SSGBerk

"; cat src/.list; } > src/README.md && rm src/.list && mdbook build'

generators.notes: Benchmarked with a minimal theme/index.hbs (no sidebar), search, print page and hosted fonts disabled. The build command regenerates SUMMARY.md and the index (README.md) from the post files before mdbook build. firstRelease from the first GitHub release (v0.0.1, 2015); the sidebar table of contents file (toc.html) is still emitted.

generators.name: Metalsmith + Handlebars
generators.description: Metalsmith is a pluggable Node.js static site generator, benchmarked here with Handlebars layouts.
generators.notes: Uses @metalsmith/markdown, @metalsmith/layouts and @metalsmith/permalinks with jstransformer-handlebars (Handlebars: https://github.com/handlebars-lang/handlebars.js, MIT).

generators.name: Metalsmith + Nunjucks
generators.description: Metalsmith is a pluggable Node.js static site generator, benchmarked here with Nunjucks layouts.
generators.notes: Uses @metalsmith/markdown, @metalsmith/layouts and @metalsmith/permalinks with jstransformer-nunjucks (Nunjucks: https://github.com/mozilla/nunjucks, BSD-2-Clause).

generators.name: Middleman
generators.description: Middleman is a Ruby static site generator that builds sites from templates, with blogging via middleman-blog.
generators.notes: Posts via middleman-blog; Markdown via kramdown. The repo has no GitHub Releases; 4.6.3 was published to RubyGems on 2026-02-16.

generators.name: MkDocs
generators.description: MkDocs is a Python static site generator for project documentation that builds a site from Markdown files and a YAML configuration.
generators.notes: Benchmarked with a minimal custom theme (single main.html) instead of the built-in themes; no plugins (search disabled). firstRelease from the first PyPI upload (0.2, 2014-01-21).

generators.name: Nanoc
generators.description: Nanoc is a flexible Ruby static site generator driven by a Rules file of filters and layouts.
generators.notes: Markdown via the kramdown filter. firstRelease from the official release notes (1.0, 2007-05-03); nanoc.app redirects to the homepage.

generators.name: Next.js (static export)
generators.description: Next.js is a React framework that, with output set to export, prerenders App Router pages to static HTML at build time.
generators.notes: firstRelease from npm next 1.0.0 (2016-10-25). Markdown is not built in: this setup parses it with gray-matter and marked inside a Server Component. Built with output: 'export' and trailingSlash.

generators.name: Nextra
generators.description: Nextra is a Next.js based static site generator that compiles Markdown and MDX content into App Router pages, best known for docs and blog themes.
generators.notes: Nextra 4.6.1 on Next.js 16.3.8, App Router, output: 'export' and trailingSlash. No Nextra theme: a bare layout and MDX wrapper render only the post; the index is a plain page listing the post slugs. Search (pagefind) is off: Nextra 4 only indexes through a separate postbuild script, which is not run. firstRelease is approximate (first nextra npm release in 2020).

generators.name: Nikola + Mako
generators.description: Nikola is a Python static website and blog generator, benchmarked here with Mako templates.
generators.notes: Nikola also supports Jinja2 themes; this variant uses Mako. firstRelease from the 1.1 git tag (2012-03-31); PyPI uploads start at 5.5 (2013).

generators.name: Nuxt Content
generators.description: Nuxt is a Vue application framework; with the Nuxt Content module it renders a folder of Markdown files into a statically generated site.
generators.notes: Nuxt 4.5.2 with @nuxt/content 3.16.1 (nuxt/content repository, first release 2020). Nuxt is an application framework; the content module makes it a Markdown site generator. Static output comes from nuxt generate.

generators.name: Observable Framework
generators.description: Observable Framework is a static site generator for data apps and dashboards that turns Markdown with reactive JavaScript cells and data loaders into static HTML.
generators.notes: Pinned @observablehq/framework 1.13.4 (latest stable on 2026-10-05). The site disables the sidebar, table of contents, pager, search, header and footer; the index lists posts through a data loader (posts.json.js) read with FileAttachment.

generators.name: Pelican
generators.description: Pelican is a Python static site generator that turns Markdown or reStructuredText content into a blog with Jinja2 templates.
generators.notes: Benchmarked with a minimal custom theme (base, article, index) instead of notmyidea. firstRelease from the 1.1 git tag (2010-08-19); PyPI uploads start in 2014.

generators.name: Publish
generators.description: Publish is a static site generator for Swift developers: a Swift package whose executable builds the site from Markdown with type-safe HTML themes.
generators.notes: The timed build runs the pre-compiled site executable, as a Publish site does on each build. Ink's metadata block cannot read the YAML tags list, so a custom publishing step parses the front matter and uses Ink for the Markdown body.

generators.name: Quarto
generators.description: Quarto is a scientific and technical publishing system built on Pandoc that renders Markdown and notebooks into websites, books and documents.
generators.notes: Benchmarked on plain markdown (no Jupyter or knitr engine). The CLI is TypeScript on Deno and drives the bundled Pandoc. License is MIT (COPYING.md; GitHub reports NOASSERTION because of the file name). firstRelease is the oldest GitHub release, v0.1.13 (2021-01-19).

generators.name: Quartz
generators.description: Quartz is a static site generator that turns Markdown notes into a fast, linked digital garden website.
generators.notes: Distributed as a repository template, so the v5.0.0 sources are vendored into src/ and their plugins are installed from the pinned commits in quartz.lock.json at image build time. GitHub's latest-release marker still points at v4.0.8 (2023); v5.0.0 (2026-03-14) is the newest tag and the default branch. firstRelease is a best-effort year for Quartz 3 (Hugo-based, 2021-2022). This setup keeps only the content, folder-listing, GFM, link and draft plugins.

generators.name: Sphinx
generators.description: Sphinx is a Python documentation generator that builds HTML sites from reStructuredText or Markdown (through MyST-Parser) sources.
generators.notes: Sphinx 9.1.0 with MyST-Parser 5.1.0 (Markdown) and a minimal custom theme (single page.html) instead of alabaster; search, genindex and source copies disabled. firstRelease from Sphinx 0.1 (2008-03-21).

generators.name: Starlight
generators.description: Starlight is a documentation theme and framework built on Astro that renders Markdown and MDX content to static HTML.
generators.notes: Runs on Astro 7.3.5. firstRelease is the year of the first @astrojs/starlight npm release (2022). This setup uses Markdown posts and one MDX index page.

generators.name: SvelteKit
generators.description: SvelteKit is the application framework for Svelte; with adapter-static and mdsvex it prerenders Markdown posts to static HTML.
generators.notes: Application framework used as an SSG through adapter-static and mdsvex (Markdown compiled to Svelte components). firstRelease from the first public SvelteKit beta (2020). Minimal site: bare layout, one post route and one index route.

generators.name: VitePress
generators.description: VitePress is a Vite and Vue powered static site generator that turns Markdown into fast static HTML pages.
generators.notes: firstRelease from npm vitepress creation (2020-04-30); the oldest GitHub release is v0.7.3 (2020-11-16). This setup uses a minimal custom theme (bare layout rendering the page content) and a createContentLoader data file for the index; no default theme, search or sidebar.

generators.name: VuePress
generators.description: VuePress is a Vue powered static site generator that turns Markdown into static HTML pages, with a Vite or webpack bundler.
generators.notes: Pinned to VuePress 2.0.0-rc.31 (no 2.x stable release exists; npm latest is 1.9.10, the v2 line ships as release candidates). Uses @vuepress/bundler-vite and a minimal local theme (one layout rendering only the page content, with a post list on the index built from a temp data file written by the theme's onPrepared hook); no default theme, navbar, sidebar or search. firstRelease from npm vuepress creation (2018-04-12).

generators.name: Zensical
generators.description: Zensical is a static site generator for project documentation from the team behind Material for MkDocs, with a Rust core and a Python package that reads MkDocs-style configuration.
generators.notes: Rust core distributed as a Python wheel; benchmarked with a minimal theme override (single main.html via theme.custom_dir) instead of the built-in Material-style theme. Search index and sitemap are always produced by the tool and counted in the output.

generators.name: Zola
generators.description: Zola is a single-binary static site generator written in Rust that renders Markdown with Tera templates.
generators.notes: firstRelease from the oldest GitHub release (v0.0.2, 2017-03-24); crates.io only starts in 2022.

proposed.notes: The issue links tlienart/Franklin.jl; GitHub redirects it to JuliaDocs/Franklin.jl (checked 2026-10-04).
